facts.fact: ANPTIC's annual report for 2020 lists town halls among the offices its regional maintenance antennas served on the State's administration network RESINA in 2020: the Dédougou town hall given a local network and RESINA access, the Fada N'Gourma town hall's network incidents resolved, network interventions (local, fibre, WiMAX) at the town halls of Tenkodogo and Manga, and sites of the Ouagadougou town hall connected to RESINA by fibre.

The report names five communes whose town halls were on or being put on RESINA in 2020 (Dédougou, Fada N'Gourma, Tenkodogo, Manga and Ouagadougou), within about 235 structures served by the antennas; it gives no total of town halls connected. Its figure of 93 commune seats reached by RESINA, 26.49 per cent, counts localities covered, not town halls.

The report says access to RESINA gives the administration's professional email, IP telephony and the Active Directory service; for the town halls it lists it states network access only, with no national application named.

RESINA is built and run for the government by ANPTIC, a state public establishment under the technical supervision of the ministry of the digital economy (MENPTD), acting as delegated contracting authority under contract-plans with the ministry.

The report gives the State of Burkina Faso as the source of finance of the RESINA reinforcement and extension project, FCFA 346.2 million in 2020, while of the FCFA 10.25 billion ANPTIC mobilised for all its projects in 2020 the state budget gave 21.4 per cent and external finance 78.6 per cent (the pylons and fibre came largely from the Luxembourg-funded PADTIC and the Danish-funded G-Cloud); it also reports persistently insufficient funds for RESINA's maintenance.
